history.period: Legendary: King Janak era; documented endowment 1869 BS (1812–13 AD)
history.summary: MAJOR CORRECTION: the famous Jaleshwar Mahadev Temple stands at Jaleswar, Mahottari district, Madhesh Province, NEPAL — not Madhubani, Bihar (it sits near the Indian border at Bhitthamore, Bihar). No 'Jaleshwar Temple' is documented in Madhubani district, Bihar — keep-or-drop/correct-location decision needed. It is the submerged-lingam temple: a square Shiva linga sits in a water tank about 20 feet below the surface, reached by a narrow stone stairway (16 stone steps), and stays immersed most of the year — the water is drained only on Maha Shivaratri and Shravan Mondays, hence 'Jaleshwar' (lord of the water). Tradition traces it to the era of King Janak; legend says soil was taken from this temple at Rama and Sita's marriage. A copper inscription records King Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah's grant of 275 bighas of land in 1869 BS (1812–13 AD) for its upkeep. The town of Jaleshwar is named after the temple.

name: Jaleshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Jaleshwar (Jaleswar) is a municipality and the district headquarters of Mahottari district in Madhesh Province, Nepal, on the Terai near the Indian border at Bhitthamore, Bihar, with a customs checkpoint; the town is named after its famous Shiva temple. (CSV lists town as Madhubani and state as Bihar — both wrong; the temple is in Nepal.)

travel.road: About 18 km south of Janakpur; Nepal Tourism Board notes about a two-hour drive from Janakpur by highway

visitor_information.best_time: Maha Shivaratri and Shravan (July–August), when the lingam becomes accessible
visitor_information.opening_hours: Lingam accessible only on festival days; general darshan hours not documented (verify)
